short: Francis Walsingham was Elizabeth I's principal secretary and spymaster, famously uncovering the Babington Plot against her.
full:
A staunchly Protestant statesman, Francis Walsingham served as Queen Elizabeth I's principal secretary from 1573 until his death. He is best remembered as the creator of a formidable domestic and international intelligence network. Utilizing double agents, cryptographers, and informers, Walsingham systematically dismantled Catholic conspiracies aimed at assassinating the queen and placing Mary, Queen of Scots on the throne.

Walsingham's most famous intelligence coup was the entrapment of Mary, Queen of Scots through the 1586 Babington Plot. By intercepting and deciphering her secret correspondence, he secured the irrefutable evidence Elizabeth needed to execute her rival. He also championed English maritime expansion and played a key role in preparing the nation's defenses against the Spanish Armada.
